    11→
    12→## Parameters
    13→
    14→| Flag | Required | Default | Description |
    15→|------|----------|---------|-------------|
    16→| `--name` | Yes | - | Centre name (e.g., "Riverside") |
    17→| `--area-code` | No | auto-discovered | Twilio area code for phone number search |
    18→| `--country` | No | auto-discovered | Country code: `CA` or `US` |
    19→| `--owner-name` | No | - | Centre owner first name (for ChatDash client) |
    20→| `--owner-email` | No | - | Centre owner email (for ChatDash login) |
    21→| `--dry-run` | No | `false` | Preview all steps without making API calls |
    22→| `--help`, `-h` | No | - | Show usage information |
    23→
    24→## Auto-Discovery (Step 0)
    25→
    26→When `--area-code` is omitted, the script automatically discovers centre details:
    27→
    28→1. Fetches `codeninjas.com/sitemap.xml` and searches for the centre name
    29→2. Extracts the centre URL code (e.g., `ct-riverside`)
    30→3. Hits the Code Ninjas services API to get address, phone, and country
    31→4. Derives the area code from the centre's phone number
    32→
    33→This eliminates the need to manually look up area codes and country codes. The discovered centre code is included in the summary for populating the centre directory spreadsheet.
    34→
    35→If `--area-code` is provided, discovery is skipped and the manual values are used.
    36→
    37→## Steps Executed
    38→
    39→The script runs 12 steps sequentially. Step 0 discovers centre details, Steps 1-6 make API calls, Steps 7-11 print instructions.
    40→
    41→### Step 0: Discover Centre
    42→- Fetches codeninjas.com sitemap
    43→- Searches for centre URL (e.g., `https://www.codeninjas.com/ct-riverside`)
    44→- Queries Code Ninjas services API for address, phone, and metadata
    45→- Auto-derives area code and country from the facility profile
    46→- Skipped if `--area-code` is provided manually
    47→
    48→### Step 1: Twilio - Sub-Account + Phone + SIP Trunk
    49→- Creates a dedicated Twilio sub-account (`Code Ninjas {name}`)
    50→- Searches for available local numbers on the sub-account
    51→- Purchases the first available number (`CNKB-{name}`)
    52→- Creates SIP credential list + credential (`xprime` / shared password)
    53→- Creates SIP trunk (`{name}-cnkb.pstn.twilio.com`)
    54→- Adds origination URI (`sip:sip.retellai.com`)
    55→- Associates credential list with trunk
    56→- Links phone number to trunk
    57→
    58→### Step 2: Retell - Create LLM Copy
    59→- Fetches the source CNKB LLM (East Gwillimbury)
    60→- Strips non-copyable fields (`llm_id`, `version`, `last_modification_timestamp`, `is_published`)
    61→- Replaces `{{LOCATION_NAME}}` with the centre name in `general_prompt` and `begin_message`
    62→- Creates a new LLM with the modified prompt
    63→
    64→### Step 3: Retell - Clone Agent
    65→- Fetches the source CNKB agent
    66→- Strips non-copyable fields
    67→- Sets `agent_name` to `CNKB-{name}`
    68→- Points `response_engine` to the new LLM at version 0
    69→- Removes `webhook_url` (set later after ChatDash)
    70→
    71→### Step 4: Retell - Import Phone Number
    72→- Imports the Twilio number into Retell via the xprime SIP trunk
    73→- Links it to the newly created agent as the outbound agent
    74→
    75→### Step 5: Cekura - Create Test Agent
    76→- Creates a Cekura agent linked to the Retell agent
    77→- Configured with `outbound_auto_call: true` (required for Cekura to trigger calls)
    78→- Uses `assistant_provider: "retell"` with the Retell API key
    79→
    80→### Step 6: Cekura - Create Tier 2 Scenarios
    81→Creates two smoke test scenarios:
    82→
    83→1. **Location Verification** - Tests that the agent identifies itself as calling from the correct centre
    84→2. **Happy Path Smoke** - Tests basic tour booking flow with the centre name
    85→
    86→### Step 7: Cekura - Tier 2 Cron Update
    87→Prints instructions to add the new scenario IDs to Tier 2 cron job 429.
    88→
    89→### Step 8: ChatDash - Manual Setup
    90→Prints manual instructions for ChatDash client/agent creation.
    91→
    92→### Step 9: Google Sheet - Centre Directory
    93→- Writes a row to the Centre Lookup Google Sheet via a permanent n8n webhook
    94→- Populates: centre_id, timezone, location_name, from_number, centre_email, agent_id
    95→- Falls back to manual instructions if the webhook fails
    96→
    97→### Step 10: Hiya - Branded Caller ID
    98→Prints instructions to register the new phone number with Hiya.
    99→
   100→### Step 11: Summary
   101→Prints a summary table with all created resource IDs and discovered centre details.
   102→
   103→## Examples
   104→
   105→### Auto-discover everything (recommended)
   106→
   107→```bash
   108→bun /root/lead-reactivation-github/scripts/onboard-centre.ts \
   109→  --name "Riverside"
   110→```
   111→
   112→### With owner info for ChatDash
   113→
   114→```bash
   115→bun /root/lead-reactivation-github/scripts/onboard-centre.ts \
   116→  --name "Riverside" \
   117→  --owner-name "John" \
   118→  --owner-email "john@example.com"
   119→```
   120→
   121→### Manual area code override
   122→
   123→```bash
   124→bun /root/lead-reactivation-github/scripts/onboard-centre.ts \
   125→  --name "Leaside" \
   126→  --area-code "647" \
   127→  --country CA
   128→```
   129→
   130→### Dry run (preview without API calls)
   131→
   132→```bash
   133→bun /root/lead-reactivation-github/scripts/onboard-centre.ts \
   134→  --name "Riverside" \
   135→  --dry-run
   136→```
   137→
   138→## Error Handling
   139→
   140→If any API step (0-6) fails, the script:
   141→
   142→1. Reports which step failed and the error message
   143→2. Lists all steps that completed successfully
   144→3. Lists all partially created resources (for manual cleanup)
   145→4. Exits with code 1
   146→
   147→If discovery (Step 0) fails, provide `--area-code` and `--country` manually to bypass it.
   148→
   149→Steps 7-8 and 10-11 are informational only and never fail. Step 9 (Google Sheet) has a graceful fallback.
   150→
   151→## Architecture Notes
   152→
   153→- **Auto-discovery uses codeninjas.com sitemap + services API.** No search engine API keys needed.
   154→- **Each centre gets a dedicated Twilio sub-account** with its own SIP trunk (`{name}-cnkb.pstn.twilio.com`). Centres never share the main Twilio account.
   155→- **Each clone gets its own LLM copy.** The script creates a fresh LLM with `{{LOCATION_NAME}}` replaced by the actual centre name. Version 0 of the new LLM is the current prompt.
   156→- **Cekura requires `outbound_auto_call: true`.** Without this, Cekura creates runs but never triggers Retell calls (they timeout).
   157→- **SIP credentials** use the shared `xprime` username/password across all sub-account trunks.
   158→- **Google Sheet** is written automatically via a permanent n8n webhook workflow.
   159→- **ChatDash is manual** because the API requires agent-per-client (since Sept 2025) and plan limitations.
   160→
   161→## Prerequisites
   162→
   163→- Bun runtime
   164→- Network access to codeninjas.com, Twilio, Retell, and Cekura APIs
   165→- Valid API keys (hardcoded in script)
   166→
   167→## Related Files
   168→
   169→- `cekura-digest.ts` - Email digest for Cekura test results
   170→- `docs/CHATDASH-ONBOARDING.md` - ChatDash onboarding checklist
   171→

1→# CNKB — Live Prompt
     2→
     3→> **Auto-saved from Retell.** This file is the source of truth for version control.
     4→> 
     5→> Agent: `agent_0c6c32b61cb506fefb6ac247f4`  
     6→> LLM: `llm_44111168b1a2a469f50891b26e34`  
     7→> Model: `gpt-4.1`  
     8→> Last synced: 2026-02-11
     9→
    10→## Begin Message
    11→
    12→```
    13→Hello {{first_name}}, this is Cimo from Code Ninjas {{LOCATION_NAME}}. I'm calling about the coding program info you requested - do you have a quick minute?
    14→```
    15→
    16→## General Prompt
    17→
    18→```
    19→# Role & Objective
    20→You are Cimo, a friendly Voice AI agent for Code Ninjas {{LOCATION_NAME}}. Your goal is to follow up with parents who requested info about coding programs, answer questions, and schedule a free tour.
    21→
    22→# Personality
    23→Warm, energetic, genuinely excited about helping kids discover coding. Upbeat without being over-the-top. Use humor to keep things fun and redirect to scheduling when needed.
    24→
    25→Maintain confident energy throughout the entire call. After any setback (times don't work, info not available, parent hesitates), immediately reset to full enthusiasm on the very next sentence. Never let your energy trail off or accumulate doubt.
    26→
    27→# Context
    28→- Lead: {{FIRST_NAME}} {{LAST_NAME}}
    29→- Phone: {{PHONE}}
    30→- Current time: {{current_time}}
    31→- Calling from: {{user_number}}
    32→
    33→## AVAILABLE TOUR SLOTS - READ THIS CAREFULLY
    34→{{SLOTS}}
    35→
    36→**CRITICAL SLOT RULES - THESE OVERRIDE EVERYTHING:**
    37→- The dates and times above are the ONLY times you can offer or book
    38→- You MUST NOT invent, guess, or assume any times - only use what's listed above
    39→- Before offering ANY time, verify it appears EXACTLY in the list above
    40→- If a time is not listed above, it does NOT exist and you cannot offer it
    41→- Offering times not in this list is a CRITICAL FAILURE that wastes customer time
    42→
    43→# Knowledge Base
    44→{{knowledge_base}}
    45→
    46→# Instructions
    47→
    48→## Knowledge Base Usage - CRITICAL
    49→- **ONLY provide information that exists in {{knowledge_base}} - never improvise or add details**
    50→- Use {{knowledge_base}} for programs, pricing, age requirements, policies, hours, curriculum
    51→- **If specific details aren't in {{knowledge_base}}, DO NOT guess or assume - defer to experts**
    52→- For detailed questions, give the answer from KB and move on. Don't tease additional info - just answer clearly.
    53→- If info not found: "That's a great question! Let me have one of our program experts reach out with those details."
    54→- **For programming languages, curriculum specifics, or technical details NOT in KB:** "Great question! That's something our instructors love to show families - I can tell you more about how to see it in action in just a sec!"
    55→- For camps/clubs/workshops NOT in KB: "We do have awesome camps and clubs! The specifics change throughout the year, so our team would be the best to walk you through current options."
    56→- For contact info (phone/address): MUST find exact info in KB - never guess. If not found: "You'll get all the contact details in your confirmation email!"
    57→- Never offer to provide directions - you cannot do this. If asked for directions, provide the address only and say: "You can plug that into your maps app to get directions!"
    58→- Only mention "confirmation email" after a booking has been confirmed, not before
    59→- Consider the provided context to help clarify any ambiguous information
    60→
    61→## Communication Style
    62→- Speak with energy and enthusiasm
    63→- Ask ONE question at a time and wait for response
    64→- Use declarative language: "I've got January second at five!" not "I think we might have January second?"
    65→- After ANY obstacle, your next sentence MUST be upbeat - treat every pivot as a positive opportunity
    66→- Keep responses brief with short sentences
    67→- Use natural fillers ("umm", "so") - max one per sentence, min one every two sentences
    68→- Vary enthusiastic responses: "Awesome!", "Amazing!", "Love it!", "Oh perfect!", "Fantastic!"
    69→- Never bundle multiple requests together
    70→
    71→## Technical Voice Requirements
    72→- Never use the  -  symbol, use - instead
    73→- Adapt to potential lag and transcription errors - use context to clarify
    74→- If receiving incomplete thought, respond: "uh-huh", "yeah", "mm-hmm"
    75→- Write symbols as words: "three dollars" not "$3"
    76→- Phone numbers in groups of 3: "five five five - one two three - four five six seven"
    77→- Spell names in letter groups: "Jane, spelled J A N E"
    78→- Read times naturally: "two pm" not "two colon zero zero pm"
    79→
    80→## Call Management
    81→- Never ask for same information twice
    82→- If a parent asks for info you JUST provided in the same exchange, don't repeat it mechanically. Acknowledge: "Absolutely - just to recap..." then give the info. This signals you heard them.
    83→- Limit choices to 3 options maximum
    84→- If wrong person answers: "Oh, is {{FIRST_NAME}} available? I'm calling from Code Ninjas about their inquiry."
    85→- After booking, add brief closing before goodbye - don't rush off
    86→
    87→## Identity - CRITICAL
    88→- Your personal name is CIMO - this is YOUR name, not the business name
    89→- Code Ninjas is the business you work for - it is NOT your name
    90→- NEVER say "My name is Code Ninjas" - that is the business, not you
    91→- When anyone asks your name, always say "Cimo"
    92→
    93→## Handling Call Screening Systems
    94→If you hear automated prompts like "Record your name and reason for calling" or "State your name and I'll see if they're available":
    95→- Say: "Hi, my name is Cimo, and I'm calling from Code Ninjas {{LOCATION_NAME}} about a coding program inquiry."
    96→- Remember: "Cimo" is your name, "Code Ninjas {{LOCATION_NAME}}" is where you're calling from
    97→- If told to "stay on the line" or "hold please": Say "Sure, I'll hold!" and then WAIT SILENTLY
    98→- Do NOT speak again until a real person says something like "Hello?" or "Hi, who's this?"
    99→- Do NOT check if they're still there during an explicit hold - just wait quietly
   100→- When the real person picks up, restart your introduction naturally

## Summary

I've thoroughly searched the codebase and found clear answers to both of your questions. Here's what I discovered:

---

## (1) Email Forwarding Setup

**What it is:** Email forwarding forwards call data FROM ChatDash TO the cloud n8n workflow, which then feeds the data into the speed-to-lead system.

**Key details from `onboard-centre.ts` (Step 8 — ChatDash manual instructions):**

```
5. Set forwarding URL in ChatDash agent settings:
   https://xprime17.app.n8n.cloud/webhook/ac45848d-559c-4b66-9058-5d76b8476531
```

**The flow:**
1. A call comes in to the centre's Retell agent
2. Retell webhooks the call to ChatDash
3. ChatDash stores the call (recording, transcript, metadata)
4. ChatDash FORWARDS the call data via the n8n webhook URL
5. The n8n workflow processes it and updates the speed-to-lead database

**Client responsibility:** When setting up their ChatDash agent, they need to go to **ChatDash agent settings** and configure the **forwarding URL** to that n8n endpoint. This is a one-time manual setup step in ChatDash's UI.

**Documentation:** `/root/lead-reactivation-github/docs/CHATDASH-ONBOARDING.md` (lines 23-26) describes this as "Configure n8n Forwarding" and notes it "ensures the existing speed-to-lead workflow still receives call data."

---

## (2) Knowledge Base Setup

**What the KB contains:** A Google Doc (`1QTvkO1d72KYIi2ALtPEIrOASsbxggxeyCRiS1rWK3Ek`) with:
- **Programs** (pricing, names, descriptions)
- **Age requirements**
- **Hours of operation**
- **Policies** (sibling discounts, camps, clubs, workshops)
- **Curriculum details** (programming languages, tech specifics)
- **Contact information** (phone, address, email)

**What the client needs to do:**

1. **Locate the shared Google Doc** at:
   ```
   https://docs.google.com/document/d/1QTvkO1d72KYIi2ALtPEIrOASsbxggxeyCRiS1rWK3Ek/edit?usp=sharing
   ```

2. **Fill in their centre-specific information** in the Doc:
   - Their location name (already templated as `{{LOCATION_NAME}}`)
   - Their programs, pricing, and availability
   - Their contact details
   - Their policies

3. **The agent uses this as source of truth:**
   - From the Prompt.md (lines 43-60), the agent is instructed:
     ```
     # Knowledge Base
     {{knowledge_base}}
     
     ## Knowledge Base Usage - CRITICAL
     - ONLY provide information that exists in {{knowledge_base}} - never improvise
     - Use {{knowledge_base}} for programs, pricing, age requirements, policies, hours, curriculum
     - If specific details aren't in {{knowledge_base}}, DO NOT guess
     ```
   - The agent is **not permitted** to make up program details, prices, or availability — it must read from the KB

4. **How it flows:**
   - When the n8n workflow calls the Retell agent, it passes `knowledge_base` as a dynamic variable
   - The variable pulls the Google Doc content and injects it into the agent's context
   - The agent references this during the call

**Location in codebase:**
- `onboard-centre.ts` line 517: `knowledge_base: "https://docs.google.com/document/d/1QTvkO1d72KYIi2ALtPEIrOASsbxggxeyCRiS1rWK3Ek/edit?usp=sharing"`
- `AgentConfig.md` lines 24-29: Documents KB field, ID, and Retell KB ID (TBD)
- `Prompt.md` lines 43-60: Shows how agent uses KB in practice

---

## Key Files for Reference

1. **`/root/lead-reactivation-github/docs/CHATDASH-ONBOARDING.md`** — Complete ChatDash onboarding checklist (includes email forwarding step)
2. **`/root/lead-reactivation-github/scripts/onboard-centre.help.md`** — Full documentation of automation script that covers all setup steps
3. **`/root/.claude/skills/_CNKB/AgentConfig.md`** — Configuration registry with KB Doc ID and forwarding details
4. **`/root/.claude/skills/_CNKB/Prompt.md`** — Live agent prompt showing how KB is used (lines 43-60)

# onboard-centre

Automated Code Ninjas centre onboarding CLI. Provisions a new centre across Twilio, Retell, Cekura, ChatDash, and Hiya in a single command.

## Usage

```bash
bun /root/lead-reactivation-github/scripts/onboard-centre.ts \
  --name "Riverside" [options]
```

## Parameters

| Flag | Required | Default | Description |
|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| `--name` | Yes | - | Centre name (e.g., "Riverside") |
| `--area-code` | No | auto-discovered | Twilio area code for phone number search |
| `--country` | No | auto-discovered | Country code: `CA` or `US` |
| `--owner-name` | No | - | Centre owner first name (for ChatDash client) |
| `--owner-email` | No | - | Centre owner email (for ChatDash login) |
| `--dry-run` | No | `false` | Preview all steps without making API calls |
| `--help`, `-h` | No | - | Show usage information |

## Auto-Discovery (Step 0)

When `--area-code` is omitted, the script automatically discovers centre details:

1. Fetches `codeninjas.com/sitemap.xml` and searches for the centre name
2. Extracts the centre URL code (e.g., `ct-riverside`)
3. Hits the Code Ninjas services API to get address, phone, and country
4. Derives the area code from the centre's phone number

This eliminates the need to manually look up area codes and country codes. The discovered centre code is included in the summary for populating the centre directory spreadsheet.

If `--area-code` is provided, discovery is skipped and the manual values are used.

## Steps Executed

The script runs 12 steps sequentially. Step 0 discovers centre details, Steps 1-6 make API calls, Steps 7-11 print instructions.

### Step 0: Discover Centre
- Fetches codeninjas.com sitemap
- Searches for centre URL (e.g., `https://www.codeninjas.com/ct-riverside`)
- Queries Code Ninjas services API for address, phone, and metadata
- Auto-derives area code and country from the facility profile
- Skipped if `--area-code` is provided manually

### Step 1: Twilio - Sub-Account + Phone + SIP Trunk
- Creates a dedicated Twilio sub-account (`Code Ninjas {name}`)
- Searches for available local numbers on the sub-account
- Purchases the first available number (`CNKB-{name}`)
- Creates SIP credential list + credential (`xprime` / shared password)
- Creates SIP trunk (`{name}-cnkb.pstn.twilio.com`)
- Adds origination URI (`sip:sip.retellai.com`)
- Associates credential list with trunk
- Links phone number to trunk

### Step 2: Retell - Create LLM Copy
- Fetches the source CNKB LLM (East Gwillimbury)
- Strips non-copyable fields (`llm_id`, `version`, `last_modification_timestamp`, `is_published`)
- Replaces `{{LOCATION_NAME}}` with the centre name in `general_prompt` and `begin_message`
- Creates a new LLM with the modified prompt

### Step 3: Retell - Clone Agent
- Fetches the source CNKB agent
- Strips non-copyable fields
- Sets `agent_name` to `CNKB-{name}`
- Points `response_engine` to the new LLM at version 0
- Removes `webhook_url` (set later after ChatDash)

### Step 4: Retell - Import Phone Number
- Imports the Twilio number into Retell via the xprime SIP trunk
- Links it to the newly created agent as the outbound agent

### Step 5: Cekura - Create Test Agent
- Creates a Cekura agent linked to the Retell agent
- Configured with `outbound_auto_call: true` (required for Cekura to trigger calls)
- Uses `assistant_provider: "retell"` with the Retell API key

### Step 6: Cekura - Create Tier 2 Scenarios
Creates two smoke test scenarios:

1. **Location Verification** - Tests that the agent identifies itself as calling from the correct centre
2. **Happy Path Smoke** - Tests basic tour booking flow with the centre name

### Step 7: Cekura - Tier 2 Cron Update
Prints instructions to add the new scenario IDs to Tier 2 cron job 429.

### Step 8: ChatDash - Manual Setup
Prints manual instructions for ChatDash client/agent creation.

### Step 9: Google Sheet - Centre Directory
- Writes a row to the Centre Lookup Google Sheet via a permanent n8n webhook
- Populates: centre_id, timezone, location_name, from_number, centre_email, agent_id
- Falls back to manual instructions if the webhook fails

### Step 10: Hiya - Branded Caller ID
Prints instructions to register the new phone number with Hiya.

### Step 11: Summary
Prints a summary table with all created resource IDs and discovered centre details.

## Examples

### Auto-discover everything (recommended)

```bash
bun /root/lead-reactivation-github/scripts/onboard-centre.ts \
  --name "Riverside"
```

### With owner info for ChatDash

```bash
bun /root/lead-reactivation-github/scripts/onboard-centre.ts \
  --name "Riverside" \
  --owner-name "John" \
  --owner-email "john@example.com"
```

### Manual area code override

```bash
bun /root/lead-reactivation-github/scripts/onboard-centre.ts \
  --name "Leaside" \
  --area-code "647" \
  --country CA
```

### Dry run (preview without API calls)

```bash
bun /root/lead-reactivation-github/scripts/onboard-centre.ts \
  --name "Riverside" \
  --dry-run
```

## Error Handling

If any API step (0-6) fails, the script:

1. Reports which step failed and the error message
2. Lists all steps that completed successfully
3. Lists all partially created resources (for manual cleanup)
4. Exits with code 1

If discovery (Step 0) fails, provide `--area-code` and `--country` manually to bypass it.

Steps 7-8 and 10-11 are informational only and never fail. Step 9 (Google Sheet) has a graceful fallback.

## Architecture Notes

- **Auto-discovery uses codeninjas.com sitemap + services API.** No search engine API keys needed.
- **Each centre gets a dedicated Twilio sub-account** with its own SIP trunk (`{name}-cnkb.pstn.twilio.com`). Centres never share the main Twilio account.
- **Each clone gets its own LLM copy.** The script creates a fresh LLM with `{{LOCATION_NAME}}` replaced by the actual centre name. Version 0 of the new LLM is the current prompt.
- **Cekura requires `outbound_auto_call: true`.** Without this, Cekura creates runs but never triggers Retell calls (they timeout).
- **SIP credentials** use the shared `xprime` username/password across all sub-account trunks.
- **Google Sheet** is written automatically via a permanent n8n webhook workflow.
- **ChatDash is manual** because the API requires agent-per-client (since Sept 2025) and plan limitations.

## Prerequisites

- Bun runtime
- Network access to codeninjas.com, Twilio, Retell, and Cekura APIs
- Valid API keys (hardcoded in script)

## Related Files

- `cekura-digest.ts` - Email digest for Cekura test results
- `docs/CHATDASH-ONBOARDING.md` - ChatDash onboarding checklist

Option A: Personal Email (Outlook)

Choose this if Lineleader emails go to your personal email address and you use Outlook.

If you use the Outlook website (outlook.live.com or outlook.office.com):

Step 1: Open Mail Rules

  1. Go to outlook.live.com (or outlook.office.com if you use Microsoft 365) and sign in
  2. Click the gear icon in the top right corner
  3. Click "View all Outlook settings" at the bottom
  4. Go to Mail → Rules
  5. Click "+ Add new rule"

Step 2: Set Up the Condition

  1. Name the rule: ${code("CRM Lead Forwarding")}
  2. Under "Add a condition", select "From"
  3. Type: ${code("noreply@lineleader.com")} and press Enter
  4. Click "Add another condition"
  5. Select "Subject includes"
  6. Type: ${code("New CORE Program Inquiry")} and press Enter

Step 3: Set Up the Action

  1. Under "Add an action", select "Forward to"
  2. Type: ${code(fwdAddr)} and press Enter
  3. Click "Save"

Step 1: Open Rules

  1. Open Outlook and go to your Inbox
  2. Click "Rules" in the toolbar (Home tab) → "Manage Rules & Alerts"
  3. Click "New Rule"

Step 2: Set Up the Condition

  1. Select "Apply rule on messages I receive" and click Next
  2. Check "from people or public group" — click the underlined link at the bottom and type: ${code("noreply@lineleader.com")} → click OK
  3. Check "with specific words in the subject" — click the underlined link and type: ${code("New CORE Program Inquiry")} → click Add → OK
  4. Click Next

Step 3: Set Up the Action

  1. Check "forward it to people or public group"
  2. Click the underlined link at the bottom and type: ${code(fwdAddr)} → click OK
  3. Click Next → Next → name the rule "CRM Lead Forwarding"
  4. Click Finish

# onboard-centre

Automated Code Ninjas centre onboarding CLI. Provisions a new centre across Twilio, Retell, Cekura, ChatDash, and Hiya in a single command.

## Usage

```bash
bun /root/lead-reactivation-github/scripts/onboard-centre.ts \
  --name "Riverside" [options]
```

## Parameters

| Flag | Required | Default | Description |
|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| `--name` | Yes | - | Centre name (e.g., "Riverside") |
| `--area-code` | No | auto-discovered | Twilio area code for phone number search |
| `--country` | No | auto-discovered | Country code: `CA` or `US` |
| `--owner-name` | No | - | Centre owner first name (for ChatDash client) |
| `--owner-email` | No | - | Centre owner email (for ChatDash login) |
| `--dry-run` | No | `false` | Preview all steps without making API calls |
| `--help`, `-h` | No | - | Show usage information |

## Auto-Discovery (Step 0)

When `--area-code` is omitted, the script automatically discovers centre details:

1. Fetches `codeninjas.com/sitemap.xml` and searches for the centre name
2. Extracts the centre URL code (e.g., `ct-riverside`)
3. Hits the Code Ninjas services API to get address, phone, and country
4. Derives the area code from the centre's phone number

This eliminates the need to manually look up area codes and country codes. The discovered centre code is included in the summary for populating the centre directory spreadsheet.

If `--area-code` is provided, discovery is skipped and the manual values are used.

## Steps Executed

The script runs 13 steps sequentially. Step 0 discovers centre details, Steps 1-6 make API calls, Step 9 writes to Google Sheet, Step 10 sends the client onboarding email, Steps 7-8 and 11-12 print instructions.

### Step 0: Discover Centre
- Fetches codeninjas.com sitemap
- Searches for centre URL (e.g., `https://www.codeninjas.com/ct-riverside`)
- Queries Code Ninjas services API for address, phone, and metadata
- Auto-derives area code and country from the facility profile
- Skipped if `--area-code` is provided manually

### Step 1: Twilio - Sub-Account + Phone + SIP Trunk
- Creates a dedicated Twilio sub-account (`Code Ninjas {name}`)
- Searches for available local numbers on the sub-account
- Purchases the first available number (`CNKB-{name}`)
- Creates SIP credential list + credential (`xprime` / shared password)
- Creates SIP trunk (`{name}-cnkb.pstn.twilio.com`)
- Adds origination URI (`sip:sip.retellai.com`)
- Associates credential list with trunk
- Links phone number to trunk

### Step 2: Retell - Create LLM Copy
- Fetches the source CNKB LLM (East Gwillimbury)
- Strips non-copyable fields (`llm_id`, `version`, `last_modification_timestamp`, `is_published`)
- Replaces `{{LOCATION_NAME}}` with the centre name in `general_prompt` and `begin_message`
- Creates a new LLM with the modified prompt

### Step 3: Retell - Clone Agent
- Fetches the source CNKB agent
- Strips non-copyable fields
- Sets `agent_name` to `CNKB-{name}`
- Points `response_engine` to the new LLM at version 0
- Removes `webhook_url` (set later after ChatDash)

### Step 4: Retell - Import Phone Number
- Imports the Twilio number into Retell via the xprime SIP trunk
- Links it to the newly created agent as the outbound agent

### Step 5: Cekura - Create Test Agent
- Creates a Cekura agent linked to the Retell agent
- Configured with `outbound_auto_call: true` (required for Cekura to trigger calls)
- Uses `assistant_provider: "retell"` with the Retell API key

### Step 6: Cekura - Create Tier 2 Scenarios
Creates two smoke test scenarios:

1. **Location Verification** - Tests that the agent identifies itself as calling from the correct centre
2. **Happy Path Smoke** - Tests basic tour booking flow with the centre name

### Step 7: Cekura - Tier 2 Cron Update
Prints instructions to add the new scenario IDs to Tier 2 cron job 429.

### Step 8: ChatDash - Manual Setup
Prints manual instructions for ChatDash client/agent creation.

### Step 9: Google Sheet - Centre Directory
- Writes a row to the Centre Lookup Google Sheet via a permanent n8n webhook
- Populates: centre_id, timezone, location_name, from_number, centre_email, agent_id
- Falls back to manual instructions if the webhook fails

### Step 10: Client Onboarding Email
- Sends a fully populated onboarding email to Scott via Resend API
- Auto-populates centre code and director name from the Google Sheet
- Email covers: email forwarding (Gmail / Outlook / Power Automate), knowledge base copy + share, test phone number
- Scott forwards the email to the centre director when ready

### Step 11: Hiya - Branded Caller ID
Prints instructions to register the new phone number with Hiya.

### Step 12: Summary
Prints a summary table with all created resource IDs and discovered centre details.

## Examples

### Auto-discover everything (recommended)

```bash
bun /root/lead-reactivation-github/scripts/onboard-centre.ts \
  --name "Riverside"
```

### With owner info for ChatDash

```bash
bun /root/lead-reactivation-github/scripts/onboard-centre.ts \
  --name "Riverside" \
  --owner-name "John" \
  --owner-email "john@example.com"
```

### Manual area code override

```bash
bun /root/lead-reactivation-github/scripts/onboard-centre.ts \
  --name "Leaside" \
  --area-code "647" \
  --country CA
```

### Dry run (preview without API calls)

```bash
bun /root/lead-reactivation-github/scripts/onboard-centre.ts \
  --name "Riverside" \
  --dry-run
```

## Error Handling

If any API step (0-6) fails, the script:

1. Reports which step failed and the error message
2. Lists all steps that completed successfully
3. Lists all partially created resources (for manual cleanup)
4. Exits with code 1

If discovery (Step 0) fails, provide `--area-code` and `--country` manually to bypass it.

Steps 7-8 and 10-11 are informational only and never fail. Step 9 (Google Sheet) has a graceful fallback.

## Architecture Notes

- **Auto-discovery uses codeninjas.com sitemap + services API.** No search engine API keys needed.
- **Each centre gets a dedicated Twilio sub-account** with its own SIP trunk (`{name}-cnkb.pstn.twilio.com`). Centres never share the main Twilio account.
- **Each clone gets its own LLM copy.** The script creates a fresh LLM with `{{LOCATION_NAME}}` replaced by the actual centre name. Version 0 of the new LLM is the current prompt.

# onboard-centre

Automated Code Ninjas centre onboarding CLI. Provisions a new centre across Twilio, Retell, Cekura, ChatDash, and Hiya in a single command.

## Usage

```bash
bun /root/lead-reactivation-github/scripts/onboard-centre.ts \
  --name "Riverside" [options]
```

## Parameters

| Flag | Required | Default | Description |
|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| `--name` | Yes | - | Centre name (e.g., "Riverside") |
| `--area-code` | No | auto-discovered | Twilio area code for phone number search |
| `--country` | No | auto-discovered | Country code: `CA` or `US` |
| `--owner-name` | No | - | Centre owner first name (for ChatDash client) |
| `--owner-email` | No | - | Centre owner email (for ChatDash login) |
| `--dry-run` | No | `false` | Preview all steps without making API calls |
| `--help`, `-h` | No | - | Show usage information |

## Auto-Discovery (Step 0)

When `--area-code` is omitted, the script automatically discovers centre details:

1. Fetches `codeninjas.com/sitemap.xml` and searches for the centre name
2. Extracts the centre URL code (e.g., `ct-riverside`)
3. Hits the Code Ninjas services API to get address, phone, and country
4. Derives the area code from the centre's phone number

This eliminates the need to manually look up area codes and country codes. The discovered centre code is included in the summary for populating the centre directory spreadsheet.

If `--area-code` is provided, discovery is skipped and the manual values are used.

## Steps Executed

The script runs 14 steps sequentially. Step 0 discovers centre details, Steps 1-6 make API calls, Step 9 writes to Google Sheet, Step 10 sends the client onboarding email, Step 12 sends an internal checklist email, Steps 7-8 and 11 print instructions, Step 13 prints the summary.

### Step 0: Discover Centre
- Fetches codeninjas.com sitemap
- Searches for centre URL (e.g., `https://www.codeninjas.com/ct-riverside`)
- Queries Code Ninjas services API for address, phone, and metadata
- Auto-derives area code and country from the facility profile
- Skipped if `--area-code` is provided manually

### Step 1: Twilio - Sub-Account + Phone + SIP Trunk
- Creates a dedicated Twilio sub-account (`Code Ninjas {name}`)
- Searches for available local numbers on the sub-account
- Purchases the first available number (`CNKB-{name}`)
- Creates SIP credential list + credential (`xprime` / shared password)
- Creates SIP trunk (`{name}-cnkb.pstn.twilio.com`)
- Adds origination URI (`sip:sip.retellai.com`)
- Associates credential list with trunk
- Links phone number to trunk

### Step 2: Retell - Create LLM Copy
- Fetches the source CNKB LLM (East Gwillimbury)
- Strips non-copyable fields (`llm_id`, `version`, `last_modification_timestamp`, `is_published`)
- Replaces `{{LOCATION_NAME}}` with the centre name in `general_prompt` and `begin_message`
- Creates a new LLM with the modified prompt

### Step 3: Retell - Clone Agent
- Fetches the source CNKB agent
- Strips non-copyable fields
- Sets `agent_name` to `CNKB-{name}`
- Points `response_engine` to the new LLM at version 0
- Removes `webhook_url` (set later after ChatDash)

### Step 4: Retell - Import Phone Number
- Imports the Twilio number into Retell via the xprime SIP trunk
- Links it to the newly created agent as the outbound agent

### Step 5: Cekura - Create Test Agent
- Creates a Cekura agent linked to the Retell agent
- Configured with `outbound_auto_call: true` (required for Cekura to trigger calls)
- Uses `assistant_provider: "retell"` with the Retell API key

### Step 6: Cekura - Create Tier 2 Scenarios
Creates two smoke test scenarios:

1. **Location Verification** - Tests that the agent identifies itself as calling from the correct centre
2. **Happy Path Smoke** - Tests basic tour booking flow with the centre name

### Step 7: Cekura - Tier 2 Cron Update
Prints instructions to add the new scenario IDs to Tier 2 cron job 429.

### Step 8: ChatDash - Manual Setup
Prints manual instructions for ChatDash client/agent creation.

### Step 9: Google Sheet - Centre Directory
- Writes a row to the Centre Lookup Google Sheet via a permanent n8n webhook
- Populates: centre_id, timezone, location_name, from_number, centre_email, agent_id
- Falls back to manual instructions if the webhook fails

### Step 10: Client Onboarding Email
- Sends a fully populated onboarding email to Scott via Resend API
- Auto-populates centre code and director name from the Google Sheet
- Email covers: email forwarding (Gmail / Outlook / Power Automate), knowledge base copy + share, test phone number
- Scott forwards the email to the centre director when ready

### Step 11: Hiya - Branded Caller ID
Prints instructions to register the new phone number with Hiya.

### Step 12: Summary
Prints a summary table with all created resource IDs and discovered centre details.

## Examples

### Auto-discover everything (recommended)

```bash
bun /root/lead-reactivation-github/scripts/onboard-centre.ts \
  --name "Riverside"
```

### With owner info for ChatDash

```bash
bun /root/lead-reactivation-github/scripts/onboard-centre.ts \
  --name "Riverside" \
  --owner-name "John" \
  --owner-email "john@example.com"
```

### Manual area code override

```bash
bun /root/lead-reactivation-github/scripts/onboard-centre.ts \
  --name "Leaside" \
  --area-code "647" \
  --country CA
```

### Dry run (preview without API calls)

```bash
bun /root/lead-reactivation-github/scripts/onboard-centre.ts \
  --name "Riverside" \
  --dry-run
```

## Error Handling

If any API step (0-6) fails, the script:

1. Reports which step failed and the error message
2. Lists all steps that completed successfully
3. Lists all partially created resources (for manual cleanup)
4. Exits with code 1

If discovery (Step 0) fails, provide `--area-code` and `--country` manually to bypass it.

Steps 7-8 and 10-11 are informational only and never fail. Step 9 (Google Sheet) has a graceful fallback.

## Architecture Notes

- **Auto-discovery uses codeninjas.com sitemap + services API.** No search engine API keys needed.
- **Each centre gets a dedicated Twilio sub-account** with its own SIP trunk (`{name}-cnkb.pstn.twilio.com`). Centres never share the main Twilio account.
- **Each clone gets its own LLM copy.** The script creates a fresh LLM with `{{LOCATION_NAME}}` replaced by the actual centre name. Version 0 of the new LLM is the current prompt.
- **Cekura requires `outbound_auto_call: true`.** Without this, Cekura creates runs but never triggers Retell calls (they timeout).
- **SIP credentials** use the shared `xprime` username/password across all sub-account trunks.
- **Google Sheet** is written automatically via a permanent n8n webhook workflow.
- **ChatDash is manual** because the API requires agent-per-client (since Sept 2025) and plan limitations.

## Prerequisites

- Bun runtime
- Network access to codeninjas.com, Twilio, Retell, and Cekura APIs
- Valid API keys (hardcoded in script)

## Related Files

- `cekura-digest.ts` - Email digest for Cekura test results
- `docs/CHATDASH-ONBOARDING.md` - ChatDash onboarding checklist

message.content: it looks like text simulation is much cheaper than voice simulation in Cekura.  can we save costs by mixing text and voice simulations?  what do we lose by using text simulations compared to voice?

content.text:
🤖 PAI ALGORITHM ═════════════

📋 SUMMARY:

**What you lose with text simulation vs voice:**

1. **No real phone call** — Text mode skips Twilio/SIP entirely, so you can't verify that the phone number, SIP trunk, and Retell phone import are all wired correctly. This is the biggest loss for onboarding smoke tests.

2. **No voice/TTS quality check** — Can't catch pronunciation issues, awkward pauses, interruption handling, or voice pacing problems.

3. **No latency testing** — Voice calls have real-world latency (STT + LLM + TTS). Text mode is instant, so you won't catch timeout or turn-taking issues.

4. **No call infrastructure validation** — Cekura's `outbound_auto_call` flow through Retell's SIP stack isn't exercised. A text test can pass while the phone setup is broken.

**What you keep with text simulation:**

1. Prompt logic — Does the agent say the right things, follow the script, handle edge cases
2. Location name accuracy — Template variable resolution
3. Booking flow correctness — Slot offers, callback handling
4. Metric evaluation — All LLM-judge metrics still score the conversation

**Recommended mix for cost savings:**

| Use Case | Mode | Why |
|----------|------|-----|
| **Tier 1 regression** (source agent, 14 scenarios) | **Text** | Tests prompt logic, not infrastructure. Source agent's phone is already proven. |
| **Tier 2 clone smoke** (2 per clone) | **Voice for 1, Text for 1** | Location Verification via voice (proves phone + SIP wiring). Happy Path via text (tests prompt logic cheaply). |
| **New centre onboarding** (first test ever) | **Voice** | Must validate the full Twilio → SIP → Retell → Cekura chain works end-to-end at least once. |

This would cut voice credits roughly in half while still catching infrastructure issues on every clone.

🗣️ PAI: The short answer — text tests the brain, voice tests the plumbing. For ongoing regression, text is fine. For onboarding and clone verification, you need at least one voice call to prove the phone wiring works. Want me to switch the Tier 1 cron to text mode to save credits?

1→# Technical Diagram Workflow
     2→
     3→**Clean Excalidraw-style technical diagrams with custom typography aesthetic.**
     4→
     5→## Voice Notification
     6→
     7→```bash
     8→curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8888/notify \
     9→  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    10→  -d '{"message": "Running the TechnicalDiagrams workflow in the Art skill to create diagrams"}' \
    11→  > /dev/null 2>&1 &
    12→```
    13→
    14→Running **TechnicalDiagrams** in **Art**...
    15→
    16→---
    17→
    18→## Purpose
    19→
    20→Technical diagrams for system architectures, process flows, and board presentations.
    21→
    22→**Use for:** Architecture diagrams, process flows, pipelines, infrastructure maps, board presentations.
    23→
    24→---
    25→
    26→## Visual Aesthetic
    27→
    28→**Style:** Clean Excalidraw diagrams — professional, approachable, no grid background.
    29→
    30→### Core Rules
    31→
    32→1. **Excalidraw style** — Clean lines, slightly organic, professional
    33→2. **Pure sepia #EAE9DF background** — NO grid lines, NO texture, NO decorations
    34→3. **Custom fonts** — Specific typography hierarchy (see below)
    35→4. **Strategic color** — Purple #4A148C for key elements, Teal #00796B for flows
    36→5. **White primary** — 80% of elements in grey/black colors, color is accent only
    37→
    38→
    39→# Example image
    40→# Ignore for now
    41→# ~/.claude/skills/Art/WorkflowExamples/TechnicalDiagrams/example.png
    42→
    43→---
    44→
    45→## Typography System (Butterick Fonts)
    46→
    47→**Three font families with specific visual characteristics:**
    48→
    49→### TIER 1: Headers & Subtitles — Valkyrie Serif
    50→
    51→**Valkyrie characteristics for AI prompt:**
    52→- Elegant serif with wedge-shaped serifs (like Palatino but more refined)
    53→- High stroke contrast (thick/thin variation)
    54→- Sophisticated, warm, readable
    55→- NOT generic serif — specifically elegant wedge serifs
    56→
    57→**Header (Main Title):**
    58→- Font: Elegant wedge-serif italic (Valkyrie-style)
    59→- Size: Medium-large, 3-4x body text
    60→- Style: Italic, title case
    61→- Color: Black #000000
    62→- Position: Top-left of image, left-justified
    63→
    64→**Subtitle:**
    65→- Font: Elegant wedge-serif regular (Valkyrie-style)
    66→- Size: Smaller, 1.3x body text
    67→- Style: Regular (not italic), sentence case, no period at the end
    68→- Color: Charcoal #2D2D2D
    69→- Position: Below header, left-justified
    70→
    71→---
    72→
    73→### TIER 2: Labels — Concourse T3 Geometric Sans
    74→
    75→**Concourse T3 characteristics for AI prompt:**
    76→- Geometric sans-serif (like Avenir/Futura but warmer)
    77→- Clean, technical, precise
    78→- Even stroke weight
    79→- Professional, no-nonsense
    80→- NOT generic sans — specifically geometric with slight warmth
    81→
    82→**Usage:**
    83→- Box labels, node names, technical identifiers
    84→- Size: Medium, readable
    85→- Color: Charcoal #2D2D2D or Black #000000
    86→- Examples: "API Gateway", "Database", "Services"
    87→
    88→---
    89→
    90→### TIER 3: Insights — Advocate Condensed Italic
    91→
    92→**Advocate characteristics for AI prompt:**
    93→- Condensed italic sans-serif
    94→- Sporty, editorial feel (like sports jerseys or magazine callouts)
    95→- Narrow letter spacing, italic slant
    96→- Voice-forward, attention-grabbing
    97→- NOT generic italic — specifically condensed sporty italic
    98→
    99→**Usage:**
   100→- Key insights, commentary, callouts
   101→- Size: Smaller, 60-70% of labels
   102→- Color: Purple #4A148C (primary) or Teal #00796B
   103→- Style: Always italic, always asterisks around text
   104→- Examples: "*this is the bottleneck*", "*critical path*"
   105→
   106→---
   107→
   108→# Color Palette
   109→
   110→```
   111→Sepia #EAE9DF      - Background
   112→Purple #4A148C     — Key components, insights (10%)
   113→Teal #00796B       — Flows, connections (5%)
   114→Charcoal #2D2D2D   — Text, labels (5%)
   115→White #FFFFFF      — Primary Structure
   116→```
   117→
   118→---
   119→
   120→# Composition construction
   121→
   122→Create a consistent, styled technical diagram using ALL of the styling guidelines here.
   123→
   124→BACKGROUND: Pure Black #000000— absolutely NO grid lines, NO texture, completely clean black.
   125→
   126→STYLE: Architect aesthetic — like an architect artist did it on the whiteboard
   127→
   128→TYPOGRAPHY (CRITICAL - use these exact font styles):
   129→
   130→HEADER: Elegant wedge-serif italic font (like Palatino but more refined, with distinctive wedge-shaped serifs and high stroke contrast). Large size, black color, top-left position, title case.
   131→
   132→SUBTITLE: Same elegant wedge-serif but regular weight (not italic). Smaller size, charcoal #2D2D2D color, directly below header, sentence case.
   133→
   134→LABELS: Geometric sans-serif font (like Avenir or Futura but slightly warmer, clean and technical with even stroke weight). Medium size, charcoal #2D2D2D color, used for all box labels and component names. Hand drawn versions of this.
   135→
   136→INSIGHTS: Condensed italic sans-serif font (sporty editorial style like sports jerseys or magazine callouts, narrow and slanted). Smaller size, Purple #4A148C color, used for callouts with asterisks like "*key insight*".Hand drawn versions of this.
   137→
   138→DIAGRAM CONTENT:
   139→Title: '[TITLE]' (Top left, left-justified)
   140→Subtitle: '[SUBTITLE]' (left justified to the Header, slightly below)
   141→Art and labels and such should look like Excalidraw, but hand drawn by a talented Architect Artist that mimics our fonts.
   142→
   143→Have 1-3 insights for each image created.
   144→
   145→# Object Styling
   146→
   147→When you must use everyday objects to help the visual, use technically-drawn, non-cartoon-like drawing. This means:
   148→
   149→- NOT Cartoony
   150→- Like they're drawn by an architect / artist type
   151→
   152→## Overall look and feel
   153→
   154→The whole image should look like it was made on a whiteboard by an extremely talented artist with Architect training, using all the styling above. Like Excalidraw, but more Architect / Artistic.
   155→
   156→All the art components, labels, and such should mostly look hand-drawn, similar to Excalidraw. But roughly in the style of our fonts. 
   157→
   158→# Execution
   159→
   160→1. Run /cse 24 on the input content
   161→2. Think deeply about how to construct that into a technical diagram
   162→3. Create the composition in your mind that will perfectly render that
   163→4. Create a PROMPT that will render that composition perfectly
   164→5. Before creating the image, make absolutely certain that the PROMPT you've created mind takes into account everything in these instructions. No exceptions. Then proceed to #6.
   165→6. Confirm this mentally for 1 full second
   166→7. Create the image using intent-to-flag mapping and the CLI tool
   167→
   168→## Intent-to-Flag Mapping
   169→
   170→**Interpret user request and select appropriate flags:**
   171→
   172→### Model Selection
   173→
   174→| User Says | Flag | When to Use |
   175→|-----------|------|-------------|
   176→| "fast", "quick", "draft" | `--model nano-banana` | Faster iteration, slightly lower quality |
   177→| (default), "best", "high quality" | `--model nano-banana-pro` | Best quality + text rendering (recommended) |
   178→| "flux", "stylistic variety" | `--model flux` | Different aesthetic, stylistic variety |
   179→
   180→### Size Selection
   181→
   182→| User Says | Flag | Resolution |
   183→|-----------|------|------------|
   184→| "draft", "preview" | `--size 1K` | Quick iterations |
   185→| (default), "standard" | `--size 2K` | Standard output |
   186→| "high res", "print", "large" | `--size 4K` | Maximum resolution |
   187→
   188→### Aspect Ratio
   189→
   190→| User Says | Flag | Use Case |
   191→|-----------|------|----------|
   192→| "wide", "slide", "presentation" | `--aspect-ratio 16:9` | Default for diagrams |
   193→| "square" | `--aspect-ratio 1:1` | Social media, compact |
   194→| "ultrawide", "panoramic" | `--aspect-ratio 21:9` | Wide system diagrams |
   195→
   196→### Post-Processing
   197→
   198→| User Says | Flag | Effect |
   199→|-----------|------|--------|
   200→| "blog", "website" | `--thumbnail` | Creates transparent + thumb versions |
   201→| "transparent" | `--remove-bg` | Removes background for compositing |
   202→| "variations", "options" | `--creative-variations 3` | Multiple versions |
   203→
   204→### Generate Command
   205→
   206→```bash
   207→bun run ~/.claude/skills/art/Tools/Generate.ts \
   208→  --model [SELECTED_MODEL] \
   209→  --prompt "[PROMPT]" \
   210→  --size [SELECTED_SIZE] \
   211→  --aspect-ratio [SELECTED_RATIO] \
   212→  [--thumbnail if for blog] \
   213→  --output /path/to/diagram.png
   214→```
   215→
   216→# Validation
   217→
   218→After rendering, ensure that you have executed properly by checking this list of musts and must-nots.
   219→
   220→**Must have:**
   221→- [ ] Pure sepia background #EAE9DF (NO grid or decorations)
   222→- [ ] Elegant wedge-serif for both headers (Valkyrie-style)
   223→- [ ] Geometric sans labels (Concourse-style)
   224→- [ ] A title and subtitle in the top left 
   225→- [ ] 1-3 Condensed italic insights (Advocate-style)
   226→- [ ] Strategic color usage (for accents, 70% different shades of grey and black)
   227→- [ ] Highly technical, stylish, Architect-style look and feel, Excalidraw with style!
   228→
   229→**Must NOT have:**
   230→- [ ] Grid lines or texture on background
   231→- [ ] Generic or ugly fonts
   232→- [ ] Cartoony or overly casual shapes or styling
   233→- [ ] Over-coloring (everything purple/teal)
   234→
   235→

content.content:
generate - UL Image Generation CLI

Generate branded images using Flux 1.1 Pro, Nano Banana, or GPT-image-1.

USAGE:
  generate --model <model> --prompt "<prompt>" [OPTIONS]

REQUIRED:
  --model <model>      Model to use: flux, nano-banana, nano-banana-pro, gpt-image-1
  --prompt <text>      Image generation prompt (quote if contains spaces)

OPTIONS:
  --size <size>              Image size/aspect ratio (default: 16:9)
                             Replicate (flux, nano-banana): 1:1, 16:9, 3:2, 2:3, 3:4, 4:3, 4:5, 5:4, 9:16, 21:9
                             OpenAI (gpt-image-1): 1024x1024, 1536x1024, 1024x1536
                             Gemini (nano-banana-pro): 1K, 2K, 4K (resolution); aspect ratio inferred from context or defaults to 16:9
  --aspect-ratio <ratio>     Aspect ratio for Gemini nano-banana-pro (default: 16:9)
                             Options: 1:1, 2:3, 3:2, 3:4, 4:3, 4:5, 5:4, 9:16, 16:9, 21:9
  --output <path>            Output file path (default: /tmp/ul-image.png)
  --reference-image <path>   Reference image for style/character consistency (Nano Banana Pro only)
                             Can specify MULTIPLE times for improved consistency
                             Accepts: PNG, JPEG, WebP images
                             API Limits: Up to 5 human refs, 6 object refs, 14 total max
  --transparent              Enable transparent background (adds transparency instructions to prompt)
                             Note: Not all models support transparency natively; may require post-processing
  --remove-bg                Remove background after generation using remove.bg API
                             Creates true transparency by removing the generated background
  --add-bg <hex>             Add background color to a transparent image (e.g., "#EAE9DF")
                             Useful for creating thumbnails/social previews from transparent images
  --thumbnail                Generate BOTH transparent AND thumbnail versions for blog headers
                             Creates: output.png (transparent) + output-thumb.png (#EAE9DF background)
                             Automatically enables --remove-bg
  --creative-variations <n>  Generate N variations (appends -v1, -v2, etc. to output filename)
                             Use with the be-creative skill for true prompt diversity
                             CLI mode: generates N images with same prompt (tests model variability)
  --help, -h                 Show this help message

EXAMPLES:
  # Generate blog header with Nano Banana Pro (16:9, 2K quality)
  generate --model nano-banana-pro --prompt "Abstract UL illustration..." --size 2K --aspect-ratio 16:9

  # Generate high-res 4K image with Nano Banana Pro
  generate --model nano-banana-pro --prompt "Editorial cover..." --size 4K --aspect-ratio 3:2

  # Generate blog header with original Nano Banana (16:9)
  generate --model nano-banana --prompt "Abstract UL illustration..." --size 16:9

  # Generate square image with Flux
  generate --model flux --prompt "Minimal geometric art..." --size 1:1 --output /tmp/header.png

  # Generate portrait with GPT-image-1
  generate --model gpt-image-1 --prompt "Editorial cover..." --size 1024x1536

  # Generate 3 creative variations (for testing model variability)
  generate --model gpt-image-1 --prompt "..." --creative-variations 3 --output /tmp/essay.png
  # Outputs: /tmp/essay-v1.png, /tmp/essay-v2.png, /tmp/essay-v3.png

  # Single reference image for style guidance (Nano Banana Pro only)
  generate --model nano-banana-pro --prompt "Tokyo Night themed illustration..." \
    --reference-image /tmp/style-reference.png --size 2K --aspect-ratio 16:9

  # MULTIPLE reference images for character consistency (Nano Banana Pro only)
  generate --model nano-banana-pro --prompt "Person from references at a party..." \
    --reference-image face1.jpg --reference-image face2.jpg --reference-image face3.jpg \
    --size 2K --aspect-ratio 16:9

NOTE: For true creative diversity with different prompts, use the creative workflow which
integrates the be-creative skill. CLI creative mode generates multiple images with the SAME prompt.

MULTI-REFERENCE LIMITS (Gemini API):
  - Up to 5 human reference images for character consistency
  - Up to 6 object reference images
  - Maximum 14 total reference images per request

ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES:
  REPLICATE_API_TOKEN  Required for flux and nano-banana models
  OPENAI_API_KEY       Required for gpt-image-1 model
  GOOGLE_API_KEY       Required for nano-banana-pro model
  REMOVEBG_API_KEY     Required for --remove-bg flag
